title: Finish the contract check every TaskQueue runs

blocks.text: Several teams plug their own `TaskQueue` implementations into the dispatcher, which is written against the interface. Last month one of them took the dispatcher down under load, and every team's own tests had been green. CI now runs `TaskQueueContract.breaches` on each implementation, and two of its checks are unfinished.

Write `rejectsNull` and `offerNeverThrows` in `src/main/java/practice/TaskQueueContract.java`. Each answers whether the queue it is given keeps that part of the contract written on `TaskQueue`, so that a queue the dispatcher can rely on is reported with no breaches and any other is reported. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: an unbounded queue that keeps every clause is reported with no breaches
a queue that accepts a null item is reported as breaking the null clause
a queue that serves the newest item first is reported as breaking the order clause
a bounded queue that answers false once it is full keeps the contract
a queue that throws once it holds a few dozen items is reported
a queue that refuses null with an exception other than NullPointerException is reported

origin.section: A Subtype May Accept More and Promise More, Never Less

concepts: A caller written against the supertype and run on every implementation is the only check of the contract; a test that uses one implementation checks only that one.
